section_C_candidate_hypotheses_falsifiab.epistemic_warning: STRICTLY FALSIFIABLE STRUCTURAL HYPOTHESES — NOT DECIPHERMENT OR PHONETIC READINGS. No individual Indus sign is assigned a proven phonetic value below.

H1_phonetic_syllabic_reencoding_abroad.statement: Circular Gulf/Mesopotamian seals (SEAL:C, n=15) and the Susa cylinder (SEAL:CY) exhibit a simultaneous statistical shift predicted by phonetic/syllabic spelling of foreign (Sumerian/Akkadian/Dilmunite/Amorite/Elamite) names — extending Rao et al. (2009 PNAS/Science), Parpola (1994), Vidale (2005), and Laursen (2010).
supporting_verified_evidence: Length-matched conditional bigram entropy H1 spikes +3.91σ on Foreign SEAL:C (1.441 vs 1.113±0.084 bits, B=5000 p=0.0002) while vocabulary V is compact (40 vs 43.45) -> higher combinatorial recombination of a reused sign pool.

Terminal entropy H_fin hits the mathematical maximum log2(15)=3.907 bits on Foreign SEAL:C (15/15 unique endings, z=+2.65, B=5000 p=0.0006) as Heartland grammatical suffixes drop from 59.9% to 6.7% (p=2.83e-5).

Controlled 2x2 natural experiment rules out both motif confounding (Heartland Gaur seals retain normal 32.4% final 740 & 59.0% suffixes vs Foreign Gaur 7.1%, p=2.74e-4) and geographic drift (Foreign Square SEAL:S seals retain normal syntax, H1 z=+1.18 n.s., H_fin z=+0.78 n.s., and exact 590->390->740 formulas).
Direction-invariant min(fwd, rev) surprisal remains overwhelmingly higher abroad (7.949 vs 5.831 bits, Mann-Whitney p=1.18e-7).
alternative_competing_hypotheses: Semi-literate or localized Dilmunite merchant pidgin / emblem drift (Laursen 2010): breakaway Harappan/Dilmunite seal cutters reusing familiar iconic signs (human figures, numerals) outside mainland grammatical rules without full syllabic encoding.
Corporate/guild-marker system (Vidale 2005): short-horned bull (Gaur) + circular seal + 091/090 encoding merchant family/trade-house identity rather than full spoken sentences.

H2_anthropomorphic_prefix_slot_091_090.statement: The 15.7x surge of the human-figure triad {090, 091, 093} on Foreign SEAL:C (12/15 = 80.0% vs 5.1% Heartland, p=2.30e-13) and the initial-prefix positioning of 091 (Twins) on 3/11 verified-direction SEAL:C seals (depressing H_init by -2.22σ, B=5000 p=0.0316) structurally mirror prefixing Mesopotamian personal-name/title markers (e.g., Sumerian Lú- 'Man of', Ur- 'Servant of', Akkadian Šu- 'He of', or Dilmunite ARAD 'Servant of').
H2_anthropomorphic_prefix_slot_091_090.critical_falsification_caveat: While 091's initial position is direction-verified (R/L on 2153.1 Luristan, 5227.1 & 5228.1 Karzakan), all three SEAL:C seals with initial 090 (147.1 Failaka, 5225.1 & 5231.1 Ur) have direction=UNK; reversing 5225.1 (090 001 -> 001 090) restores 090 to terminal position matching verified-R/L Failaka 148.1 (... 001->090) and unprovenanced Gulf seal 5223.1 (... 001->090). However, 090 is still unambiguously MEDIAL on verified Qala'at al-Bahrain 3863.1 (L/R) and Susa 3881.1 (R/L), confirming partial syntactic displacement.

structural_constraints: Longest complete circular Gulf seal (7 signs); anomalous in BOTH reading directions.
Exact periodic sign reduplication of 055 (12-strokes) at slots 4 & 7: [071-031-831]-055-[121-099]-055 (3+1+2+1 two-clause symmetry!).
Contains two ultra-rare anthropomorphic figures (121 & 099, each freq=2 in entire 5,679 corpus) + Gulf-enriched 831 (16.7x, shared with Luristan 2153.1).
Cuneiform structural parallel (length & bimorphemic repetition): matches a 6–7 sign two-part Dilmunite/Akkadian seal legend ([PN] + [patronymic/title] or repeated syllable/case marker -X ... -X).
Contains Gulf-exclusive bigram 055 -> 090 (0 occurrences in entire Indus Heartland; shared ONLY with unprovenanced cylinder seal 3888.1).
Initial 190 (spider/insect) is shared with unprovenanced circular seal 3887.1 (190-091-603); terminal 160 (yoke-carrier) is shared with unprovenanced Gulf Gaur seal 5223.1.
5-sign length with zero Heartland suffixes aligns with a 4–5 syllable Dilmunite/Akkadian name (cf. Ilī-ippašra, Inzak-gāmil, Šu-ilīšu).

H3_seal_by_seal_structural_constraint_ma.type_motif: All SEAL:C · Gaur (except Saar blank) · R/L · Complete
structural_constraints: Three independent complete circular Gaur seals share an identical 4-sign prefixing frame [091 + X + Y + Z] (and 5229.1 embeds [091 + 001 + 093 + 031] right after [055-220]!).
Notably, 5227.1, 5228.1, and 5229.1 all place a stroke numeral immediately after 091 (091->031, 091->032, 091->001) — a pattern appearing only ONCE in the entire 4,531-line Heartland (Harappa 697.1).
Structurally matches a 1-morpheme human/title prefix (Lú- / Ur- / Šu- / guild marker) + 3-sign personal name or numeral-qualified trade title.
BOTH 8-sign square seals found thousands of kilometers apart terminate in the exact #1 Heartland trigram 590 -> 390 -> 740 (preceded by plain fish 220 in Kish and 220->125 in Gonur Depe).

Provides a decisive falsification control: authentic Harappan merchants carrying square seals abroad kept 100% canonical Heartland suffix syntax. Therefore, the high surprisal of circular SEAL:C seals is NOT an artifact of distance or sample noise.
